Power (sensitivity) for a given design

Source: R/power_for.R
power_for.Rd

Estimates the power of a differential network analysis at a given sample size and feature count, where power is the sensitivity – the fraction of truly differential edges recovered – at a false-discovery-rate target. The achieved FDR is reported alongside, because several methods are not calibrated in every regime.

Usage

power_for(
  p,
  n,
  method,
  perturbation = "structural",
  fdr = .HOWBIG_FDR_TARGET,
  scenario = "default",
  simulate = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

p

Number of features.

n

Per-group sample size; a single number, or c(n1, n2) for unequal groups. Group 1 is the reference group (its network is intact; group 2 carries the change), so order matters.

method

Estimation method label. See howbig_methods().

perturbation

Type of differential signal: "structural" (edges appear/disappear), "magnitude" (edge strengths change), or "both".

fdr

Target false-discovery rate. The grid is scored at 0.05; other targets require simulation.

scenario

Assumption about the networks and data, for checking how sensitive an answer is to them. "default" (block-structured Barabasi-Albert tree networks, Gaussian data, empirical edge weights) is the main grid. The others are in the grid only at p = 100, n = 1000 with a structural change: "scale_free" (denser Barabasi-Albert blocks), "erdos_renyi" (random blocks), "ar1_banded" (non-modular banded network), "censored_5", "censored_25", "censored_50" (that share of each feature's values set to zero, as at a detection limit), and "uniform_weights".

simulate

If TRUE, answer off-grid designs by on-demand simulation (slow; default scenario and simulatable methods only). If FALSE (default), they are flagged instead.

...

Passed to simulate_power() when simulating (e.g. reps, n_perm, cores, seed).

Value

An object of class howbig_power: a list with the sensitivity estimate and 80% band, achieved FDR, AUPR, the number of truly differential edges, provenance, and any notes.

Details

Answers come from a precomputed simulation grid where possible. Queries that hit a grid cell are exact; queries on a swept arm are interpolated. Anything else (other designs, other unequal group sizes, FDR targets other than the grid's 0.05) is flagged simulate_required, and answered by an on-demand simulation when simulate = TRUE (see simulate_power()).

Examples

power_for(p = 250, n = 1000, method = "JGL_BIC")
#> howbig power estimate  [in-grid]
#>   JGL_BIC | structural perturbation | p = 250, n = 1000
#>   Truly differential edges: ~50 of 31,125 pairs (0.16%)
#>   Sensitivity @ FDR 0.05:  0.60   (80% band 0.50–0.70)
#>   Achieved FDR:            0.059 ✓
#>   AUPR (threshold-free):   0.68
#>   based on 100 reps
power_for(p = 250, n = 1500, method = "JGL_BIC")          # interpolated
#> howbig power estimate  [interpolated]
#>   JGL_BIC | structural perturbation | p = 250, n = 1500
#>   Truly differential edges: ~50 of 31,125 pairs (0.16%)
#>   Sensitivity @ FDR 0.05:  0.66   (80% band 0.56–0.77)
#>   Achieved FDR:            0.063 ✓
#>   AUPR (threshold-free):   0.73
power_for(p = 100, n = c(500, 1500), method = "JGL_BIC")  # unequal groups
#> howbig power estimate  [in-grid]
#>   JGL_BIC | structural perturbation | p = 100, n = 500 / 1500
#>   Truly differential edges: ~45 of 4,950 pairs (0.92%)
#>   Sensitivity @ FDR 0.05:  0.62   (80% band 0.51–0.75)
#>   Achieved FDR:            0.047 ✓
#>   AUPR (threshold-free):   0.75
#>   based on 100 reps
power_for(p = 100, n = 1000, method = "JGL_BIC", scenario = "censored_25")
#> howbig power estimate  [in-grid]
#>   JGL_BIC | structural perturbation | p = 100, n = 1000 | scenario: censored_25
#>   Truly differential edges: ~45 of 4,950 pairs (0.92%)
#>   Sensitivity @ FDR 0.05:  0.65   (80% band 0.53–0.76)
#>   Achieved FDR:            0.092 ✓
#>   AUPR (threshold-free):   0.75
#>   based on 100 reps
power_for(p = 150, n = 1500, method = "JGL_BIC")          # off-grid: flagged
#> howbig power estimate  [OFF-GRID]
#>   JGL_BIC | structural perturbation | p = 150, n = 1500
#>   Not available from the grid.
#> note: not answerable from the grid: (p = 150, n = 1500) is off the grid
#>         for the structural perturbation.
#> note: rerun with simulate = TRUE to simulate this design (slow; see
#>         ?simulate_power).
